title: Every dg module admits a surjection from a dg module with finitely generated free quotients
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-good-quotient at source lines 2489-2502: for a differential graded algebra A and any dg A-module M there is a homomorphism P -> M of dg A-modules which is surjective, whose restriction to the cycles Ker(d_P) -> Ker(d_M) is still surjective, and where P sits in an admissible short exact sequence with the outer terms direct sums of shifts of A. The proof at source lines 2504-2516 is a construction with a designed gadget rather than a citation: it builds the two-generator dg module P_k with generators in adjacent degrees k and k+1 and differential sending the first to the second, uses it to produce a surjection onto M from a direct sum of copies of P_k (which automatically gives the admissible short exact sequence of clause (3)), and then has to handle clause (2) separately by observing that a cycle of M of degree k admits a map from A[k] sending 1 to it, so that adding a direct sum of shifts of A upgrades the surjectivity on cycles. The piece that is doing the work is the gadget P_k and the fact that the added shifts do not disturb clause (3); the statement shows neither. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
